hints: Focus on what type of bonding allows conduction in the liquid state, ionic with mobile ions or covalent with no ions?
Work out what X, Y and Z are from their shells: Y with 2,8,1 loses one electron, while X with 2,6 gains two and Z with 2,8,7 gains one.
Check each formula to see if it pairs a metal with a non-metal to make an ionic lattice, or two non-metals to make a covalent molecule.
walkthrough:
**Identify X, Y and Z from electron shells**

Think of shells as telling you the group. Losing or gaining electrons to get a full outer shell tells you the ion charge.

$Y = 2,8,1$ is like sodium, Group I, forms $Y^{+}$. $X = 2,6$ is like oxygen, Group VI, forms $X^{2-}$. $Z = 2,8,7$ is like chlorine, Group VII, forms $Z^{-}$.

**Recall when liquids conduct electricity**

Ionic compounds have a giant lattice of ions. Solid they cannot move, but liquid (molten) the ions are free to move and carry charge, so they conduct.

Covalent molecular compounds have neutral molecules with no free ions or electrons, so even as liquids they do not conduct.

**Test compounds 1, 2 and 3**

1. $YZ$ is $Y^{+}$ with $Z^{-}$, like $NaCl$. Metal plus non-metal, so ionic and conducts when liquid. Correct.

2. $Y_{2}X$ is $2 \times Y^{+}$ with $X^{2-}$, like $Na_{2}O$. Metal plus non-metal, so ionic and conducts when liquid. Correct.

3. $Z_{2}X$ is two non-metals, like $Cl_{2}O$. Sharing electrons gives covalent molecules with no mobile ions, so it does not conduct. Incorrect.

So only 1 and 2 conduct.

options.A: This would mean 1, 2 and 3 all conduct. 1 and 2 are ionic and do conduct, but 3 ($Z_{2}X$) is between two non-metals (Group VII and Group VI) so it is covalent molecular and has no mobile ions in the liquid.
options.B: This is 1 and 2 only. $YZ$ ($NaCl$ type) and $Y_{2}X$ ($Na_{2}O$ type) are both metal plus non-metal ionic compounds, so their liquids contain mobile $Y^{+}$, $Z^{-}$ and $X^{2-}$ ions and conduct electricity.
options.C: This would mean 2 and 3 conduct. 2 is correct as ionic $Y_{2}X$, but 3 is wrong because $Z_{2}X$ is covalent, and it wrongly leaves out 1 which is clearly ionic $YZ$.
options.D: This would mean only 1 conducts. 1 is correct, but it wrongly leaves out 2. $Y_{2}X$ balances $2(Y^{+})$ with $X^{2-}$ to give a neutral ionic compound that also conducts when molten.
